text:
maria: Heads-up — we're seeing elevated packet loss and pod evictions in usw2-c. gc-gpu-usw2c node pool shows ~20% eviction rate and kube-proxy flaps (~30s timeouts). Planning a zonal evacuation but want a graceful sequencing plan to avoid overloading usw2-a/b and to keep model cache warm. Proposal:
1) mark nodes draining in small batches (10% at a time)
2) shift API weights incrementally (70/15/15 -> 60/20/20 -> ...)
3) pre-warm KV/prefix caches on target pools with synthetic requests
4) suspend large batch/quantization jobs for the window
Anyone see issues or different suggestions?

kevin: +1 to sequencing. Also suggest spinning up dedicated burst instances in usw2-a/b (reserved/dedicated pools) and bumping cluster-autoscaler min by +20% for 15m so we don't get scaling lag.

sam: We can run the cache-warm via /internal/kv-warm endpoint. Plan: synthetic 5rps per host for 3m, with small model calls to populate KV and KV-cache. Also recommend routing latency-sensitive traffic to prefer local if possible during the window.

jess: I'll own the drain sequencing. Quick plan and commands I'll run: 
```
# label + drain one node at a time in 10% batches
kubectl label node gc-gpu-usw2c-<id> draining=true
kubectl drain gc-gpu-usw2c-<id> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```
I'll check for CrashLoopBackOffs and reschedule windows if pods fail to start.

maria: Also need an API gateway weight change plan. Start with 70% usw2c, 15% usw2a, 15% usw2b then iterate down 10% from usw2c per batch. Kevin — can you push Envoy weight changes slowly?

kevin: On it. Will push envoy config with gradual host reconnects (throttle 5s per host) to avoid mass reconnect storms. Applying in ~2m.

ops-rotation: FYI — opened incident INC-2026-374 and paged infra. Cloud provider ticket created: CLD-9981. Marking SEV3 for now.

infra-bot: autoscaler: increased min_replicas for gc-gpu-usw2a to 24 (was 20). action_id=autoscaler_update time=1823456798

sam: Heads-up — we should pause nightly quantization and long-running eval jobs that spike disk I/O. I'll message Matt's team to pause. @jess can you pause any local batch queues you control?

jess: Pausing job queue now: `./ops pause-queue quantize-large` — confirmed.

maria: Cache-warm started (synthetic). Running 5rps across candidate hosts for 3m. Watch token fill rates and 95th latencies; continue if 95p < 80ms.

kevin: Envoy weights applied: 70/15/15. Rolling restart in progress. ETA ~8m for the rollout stabilization.

ops-rotation: Early status: after first 10% drain we saw CPU bump in usw2a but overall p95 latency still within SLOs. Proceeding with next drain batch when cache_warm completes. Next sync in 7m.

sam: Noting spot preempt churn increased on some nodes — for critical endpoints we should prefer reserved/dedicated instances; also enable cpu-fallback small model for non-critical batch to avoid queue blowups.

jess: Confirmed: first 10% batch done, no failed pods to report. Scheduling next 20% batch in 3m.

maria: If cloud tells us the network flap persists we'll abort and switch to full failover (stop accepting new connections in usw2c). For now we proceed with gradual evacuation. Thanks all :thumbsup: 

kevin: I'll keep an eye on connection resets and upstream health. Posting logs to the incident ticket.

infra-bot: note: autoscaler-check passed; new instance spin-up events observed in usw2a/usw2b.

ops-rotation: Next update after the second batch. If anyone sees >5% failed pod starts or p95 jump >100ms, call stop and we revert weights.

maria: A few followups: someone please add cache-warm verification to the incident notes (how many prefixes warmed, token counts). Also log cost impact (extra reserved/burst instances) for postmortem.

kevin: Acknowledged, I'll capture cost delta and add to INC-2026-374.
